newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds vault resistance but still on shaky ground.
newsitem.headline: Bunds vault resistance but still on shaky ground.

text.p: German Bunds firmed in early trade on Friday, buoyed by overnight gains in U.S. Treasuries and by general at the market's resilience following the victory of the Socialist-led left in Sunday's French election.
June Bund futures vaulted key resistance at 101.00 to rise as high as 101.10, but dealers doubted the market was in a mood for further big gains.
The Bundesbank's gold clash with Bonn and fears that the new French government was more sceptical about European monetary union remained as risk factors for Bunds.
"We're at a decent level but it's also a shaky level because of the gold dispute," one trader said.
He predicted June Bund futures would trade in a range of 100.50 to 101.10 today.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's Frankfurt futures trading team wrote in a note to investors:
"The bearish threats are still there, and many market participants are unlikely to make big bullish bets until the various situations start to find some resolution."
Peter Hintze, general secretary of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), said the government was confident it could reach a consensus agreement with the Bundesbank on the gold plan.
